readme:
# Job Feed - Global Multi-Platform Job Aggregator

Aggregate jobs from 109+ job boards, 26+ ATS career systems and any company website into one canonical schema. Support for more job boards and career systems is added continuously. Returns title, company, location, salary, employment type, full description, apply URL, tech stack, requirements, and a cross-source dedup key (`job_id`). No login required. Pay-per-event.

One input, one normalized schema, one stable `job_id` you can upsert on. Instead of wiring 20 separate scrapers, writing your own dedup, and reconciling 20 different field names:

1. Pick a country (or several) or hand-pick platforms.
2. Set your keywords.
3. Get one clean deduplicated feed with cross-source enrichment, cost report, overlap matrix, and search-relevance signal.

Job Feed is an orchestrator over three tiers of scrapers:

1. **109+ job boards**, each with a scraper built per site ([LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/jobs/), [Indeed](https://www.indeed.com/), [StepStone](https://www.stepstone.de/), [Jobs.ch](https://www.jobs.ch/), [Arbeitsagentur.de](https://www.arbeitsagentur.de/), [USAJOBS](https://www.usajobs.gov/), and 100+ more). Support for more job boards is added continuously. Selected via `platforms` or `countries`.
2. **`career-site-jobs`** - direct extraction from 26+ ATS career systems ([Greenhouse](https://www.greenhouse.io/), [Lever](https://www.lever.co/), [Workday](https://www.workday.com/), [Ashby](https://www.ashbyhq.com/), [Teamtailor](https://www.teamtailor.com/), [Personio](https://www.personio.com/), [SmartRecruiters](https://www.smartrecruiters.com/), [BambooHR](https://www.bamboohr.com/), [iCIMS](https://www.icims.com/), [Recruitee](https://recruitee.com/), and more). Support for more career systems is added continuously. Activated when a `companyUrls` entry matches a known ATS, or explicitly with `includeCareerSites: true`.
3. **`website-job-extractor`** - reads any other company website: it finds the careers page, detects the ATS, and falls back to LLM extraction plus a browser retry for JS-rendered sites. The catch-all when neither a dedicated scraper nor an ATS pattern fits.

## Use with AI Agents (MCP)

Connect this actor to any MCP-compatible AI client: Claude Desktop, Claude.ai, Cursor, VS Code, LangChain, LlamaIndex, or custom agents.

**Apify MCP server URL:**

```
https://mcp.apify.com?tools=santamaria-automations/job-feed
```

**Example prompt once connected:**

> "Use `job-feed` to find Software Engineer jobs in Berlin across all German platforms. Return results sorted by posted date as a table with title, company, salary, and apply URL."

Clients that support dynamic tool discovery (Claude.ai, VS Code) receive the full input schema automatically via `add-actor`.

## Quick start

```json
{
  "countries": ["DE", "AT", "CH"],
  "keywords": ["Software Engineer"],
  "maxResultsPerQueryPerPlatform": 25
}
```

That fires every Tier 1 platform in DACH, plus Indeed, Glassdoor, and LinkedIn once per country (via `includeGlobalBoards`, on by default), streams deduplicated results as they arrive, and makes four terminal items available in the run's **OUTPUT key-value-store record** once it finishes (`run_summary`, `cost_report`, `relevance_report`, `sources_manifest`), see [Terminal items](#terminal-items-in-the-output-record).

## Constraints

- **Platforms per run:** 113 selectable in the `platforms` picker; the orchestrator gates concurrency against a RAM budget, capped by `maxTotalMemoryMbytes` if you set it (see [RAM and parallelism](#ram-and-parallelism)). Browser-tier actors (Camoufox) use up to 4 GB each and queue when budget is tight, largest request admitted first as RAM frees up.
- **Sub-actor timeout:** 60-3600 seconds per platform (default 600). Slow platforms are dropped and flagged in `run_summary`, they do not block the rest of the run.
- **titleFilter:** comma-separated substring list, case-insensitive OR match. Two execution paths: platforms that declare native title-filter support (10 platforms today, see [titleFilter](#platform-selection)) get the value forwarded and filter before detail-fetch, at no extra cost; every other platform gets filtered client-side in the merge step. `dropped_title_filter` on `run_summary` reports how many rows the client-side path dropped.
- **postedWithinDays precision:** accepts fractional days: `0.5` = last 12 hours, `0.042` is roughly 1 hour, use `1.0/24` for exactly 1 hour. Platforms with native age filtering get the value forwarded directly; the rest are filtered after normalization.
- **Dedup mode:** `streaming` (default, rows flow as each platform finishes) or `batch` (buffer until all platforms complete, then emit once per unique `job_id` with all sources inline). See [Dedup mode](#dedup-mode).

## Supported platforms

127 platforms are tracked in the registry. 113 are healthy and selectable in the `platforms` picker: 110 job boards plus 3 company-website sources (`career-site-jobs`, `website-job-extractor`, `website-job-extractor-browser`). The other 14 registry entries are parked (8) or deliberately excluded (6) and never selectable (mostly aggregator wrappers over sources this fleet already scrapes first-party, such as Adzuna, Jooble, Careerjet, and Monster). See [Coming soon](#coming-soon) for what is in the build queue.

Every board has a `tier`: **Tier 1** boards run automatically when their country is in `countries[]`; **Tier 2** boards run only when named in `platforms[]`. The full list, with each board's standalone Apify actor, RAM and pricing, is in [Supported boards](#supported-boards).

### Country presets

`countries: ["XX"]` turns on every healthy Tier 1 board for that market (table below). It is additive across countries, and additive with anything you list in `platforms[]`. Tier 2 boards of a country (for example `stellenmarkt-de`, `westjob-at`, or the regional Swiss boards such as `jobbasel-ch` and `ostjob-ch`) are not in the preset and need to be named explicitly. `GB` is accepted as an alias for `UK`. Countries not in the table have no preset, use `platforms` instead.

`includeGlobalBoards` (**default `true`**) additionally runs [Indeed](https://www.indeed.com/), [Glassdoor](https://www.glassdoor.com/), and [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/jobs/) once **per selected country**: `countries: ["DE","AT"]` fires two Indeed runs, one scoped to DE and one to AT. The `maxResultsPerPlatform` cap is split across those per-country runs so the shares sum to the original cap (`10` over 3 countries gives `[4, 3, 3]`, remainder to the alphabetically first codes). Boards you name in `platforms[]` are not added twice. The flag has no effect when you select by `platforms` only, and an empty `{}` input does not trigger it. Set it to `false` to run only the preset.

### RAM and parallelism

Your Apify account has one memory limit shared by every run on it, not just those job-feed starts, so job-feed budgets sub-actor RAM instead of ignoring it. It first tries to detect the memory actually available (`GET /v2/users/me/limits`, then `GET /v2/users/me`). If you set `maxTotalMemoryMbytes`, the lower of your value and the detected figure wins. If detection is not possible it uses a flat 4096 MB, which fits every plan including Free. job-feed itself adds 256 MB on top.

Each selected board requests the RAM shown in the table above. Boards that fit start immediately, the rest wait, and as RAM frees up the largest waiting request that fits is admitted first so big browser-tier boards are not starved behind small ones. A board whose own need exceeds the whole budget fails fast with `insufficient memory budget`.

Example: ten 128 MB boards plus one 2048 MB board fit the default budget and all start in parallel. Add several 4096 MB browser-tier boards and the first starts while the rest queue. With `maxTotalMemoryMbytes: 16384` on a plan that has the RAM, those boards run side by side.

## Limitations

- **Some boards sort by relevance only.** Without a native date sort, `sortBy: "newest"` is a best-effort freshness filter over relevance-ordered results.
- **`remoteco` is parked.** remote.co hides employer data behind a paywall, so it is not selectable (see [Coming soon](#coming-soon)).
- **`wellfound-us` costs more per result** ($0.006 per listing, plus $0.010 with job details) because every request goes through an anti-bot unblocking proxy.
- **URL-only platforms need a URL.** `career-site-jobs`, `website-job-extractor`, and `website-job-extractor-browser` do nothing without `companyUrls`, `careerSites`, or `searchUrls`. If your whole selection is made of them and none is supplied (for example `includeCareerSites: true` alone), the run is rejected at input validation: exit code 2, `statusMessage` starting `"FAILED: "`, nothing dispatched or billed.
- **The browser retry has no guaranteed win.** It re-runs a zero-job URL through an extractor roughly 3-5x more expensive. You can pay for it and still get zero jobs if the content is not there (login wall, geofence, malformed feed). See [Picking HTTP or browser](#picking-http-or-browser).

## Input reference

The input schema carries a tooltip for every field. This section covers defaults and the gotchas.

### Platform selection

- **`countries[]`** - ISO codes with a preset (see [Country presets](#country-presets)). Activates each country's Tier 1 boards.
- **`platforms[]`** - hand-picked board IDs. Additive to `countries`. Tier 2 boards run only when named here.
- **`includeGlobalBoards`** - default `true`, see [Country presets](#country-presets).
- **`keywords[]`** - search terms, each forwarded to every selected board. Results are deduplicated across keywords and boards, and `matched_query` on each row records which keyword found it. Aliases `searchQueries`, `search_queries`, and `queries` are folded into `keywords` when it is empty; an explicit `keywords` always wins. `remoteco` has no free-text search, so keywords are mapped onto its 16 fixed categories (unmapped keywords are dropped with a logged warning).
- **`location`** - city, region, or state, forwarded in whatever form each board accepts. See [Location and language](#location-and-language).
- **`radiusKm`** - search radius, default 25, max 200, clamped to each board's own maximum.
- **`sortBy`** - `"newest"` (default, best for scheduled scrapes), `"relevance"`, `"salary"`, or `""` (forward nothing, board default order). A board that does not know the value ignores it.
- **`titleFilter`** - comma-separated substrings, case-insensitive OR match on `title`, for example `"sales manager, account executive"`. Ten boards filter natively before detail fetch at no extra cost (`arbeitsagentur-de`, `stepstone-de`, `france-travail`, `pracuj-pl`, `indeed`, `linkedin`, `sepe-es`, `prospects-uk`, `milkround-uk`, `nationale-vacaturebank-nl`); all others are filtered client-side after fetch, counted as `dropped_title_filter`.
- **`postedWithinDays`** - fractional days (`0` = off, `0.5` = 12 hours). Boards with a native age filter get it forwarded (rounded up to their unit), for the rest rows outside the window are dropped after normalization, counted as `dropped_stale`.
- **`searchUrls[]`** - direct search URLs for advanced use, routed to the board or ATS that matches the URL.

### Result caps

Three caps, applied from the inside out:

1. **`maxResultsPerQueryPerPlatform`** - raw rows per keyword per board. Alias `maxResultsPerQuery`. When above 0 it wins over cap 2.
2. **`maxResultsPerPlatform`** - raw rows per board across all keywords, before dedup. Alias `maxResults`. With several keywords and cap 1 at 0, each keyword gets `ceil(cap / keywords)` (3 keywords against 10 gives 4 each, so up to 12 raw rows). 0 = each board's own default.
3. **`maxResultsTotal`** - unique jobs delivered after dedup, across all boards. Once reached, job-feed stops accepting and billing further jobs. Sub-actor calls already running still finish, but their extra rows are dropped and never billed by job-feed. 0 = unlimited.

To avoid paying for rows it would then discard, job-feed also clamps the per-query cap sent to each board to `max(1, floor(maxResultsTotal / (boards * keywords)))`. A bare `{}` input shares a 50-row total across 8 boards, so each is capped at 6. If a run mixes boards with `companyUrls`, the boards see half of `maxResultsTotal` for this split.

On a `companyUrls` or `careerSites` run, `maxResultsPerPlatform` is a per-extractor budget split across its companies with `max(1, floor(cap / companies))`. Six rows over 2 companies gives 3 each (forwarded as `maxJobsPerCompany` to `career-site-jobs` and `maxResultsPerCompany` to the extractors). With more companies than the cap, every company still gets 1, so the total can run slightly over budget in that one case. Rows beyond a company's share are trimmed, never billed by job-feed, and counted as `dropped_over_cap` (see [Company career pages](#company-career-pages)).

A misspelled field name appears in the run log as `WARN input contains unrecognized keys`. Check it if a cap seems to be ignored.

### Content options

- **`includeJobDetails`** - fetch the full description, salary, and requirements from each detail page. Some boards charge more per detail than per SERP row. Off by default.
- **`includeContactData`** - fill `contacts[]` (recruiter name, email, phone) where the source has them. Implies `includeJobDetails`. About 28 boards expose contacts.
- **`includeCompanyDetails`** - fetch company profiles (`about`, `industry`, `size_range`, `social_urls`, `active_jobs`, and more). Implies `includeJobDetails`. About 28 boards support it.
- **`includeCompaniesWithoutJobs`** - default `true`, adds free zero-job company rows, see [Zero-job company rows](#zero-job-company-rows).
- **`minRelevanceScore`** - 0-100, default 0 (keep all). Each keyword is scored as the share of its tokens found in the title (case and umlaut folded), and a row scores as its best keyword. 50 drops rows where fewer than half of the best keyword's tokens match, 100 keeps only rows where every token of some keyword matches.
- **`includeReportRowsInDataset`** - default `false`, see [Terminal items in the OUTPUT record](#terminal-items-in-the-output-record).

### Company career pages

Three sub-actors can read a company career page:

| Actor | Reads | Browser or LLM | Roughly |
|---|---|---|---|
| `career-site-jobs` | Pages on a known job system (Greenhouse, Workday, Lever, Workable, and 22 more) | No | $0.001/job |
| `website-job-extractor` | Any career page over plain HTTP | LLM, managed by default | $0.012/job managed, plus $0.01/company |
| `website-job-extractor-browser` | Any career page, including JS-only apps | Real browser and LLM | roughly 3-5x the HTTP rate |

`career-site-jobs` is always cheapest when it applies. Two inputs feed it:

- **`companyUrls[]`** - one career-page URL per company. Each is checked against known ATS fingerprints (Greenhouse, Lever, Workday, Ashby, Personio, and 20+ more). A match goes to `career-site-jobs` directly (regardless of `platforms`, no API key needed), anything else to the extractor (see [Picking HTTP or browser](#picking-http-or-browser)).
- **`careerSites[]`** - for companies whose job system you already know, for example from `next_run_input`. Each entry is a plain URL (auto-detected) or `{"url": "...", "ats": "...", "company": "..."}` to skip detection. Supported `ats` values: `adp`, `ashby`, `avature`, `bamboohr`, `brassring`, `comeet`, `eightfold`, `greenhouse`, `icims`, `icims_jibe`, `jazzhr`, `join`, `lever`, `oracle_recruiting` (or `oracle`), `personio`, `phenom`, `pinpoint`, `recruitee`, `rippling`, `smartrecruiters`, `successfactors_rmk` (or `successfactors`), `talentbrew`, `taleo`, `teamtailor`, `workable`, `workday`. `icims_jibe` must be named explicitly because its tenants use custom domains. An entry with an unknown or unsupported `ats` falls back to the extractor with a logged warning. `careerSites` works on its own. Set `company` (for example `"oracle.com"`) whenever you know it, since the tenant host often names the ATS vendor, not the company. Set `country` (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, for example `"CH"`) on a single-country tenant whose list rows carry no location: unresolved rows get that country, rows with a known other country are still dropped (career-site-jobs only; an invalid code is ignored with a warning). Posting URLs are collapsed to their board URL, job-alert pages are dropped, and session parameters are stripped before dispatch.
- **`includeCareerSites`** - default `false`. Turns on `career-site-jobs` without a matching URL. It has no keyword search: with no `companyUrls`, `careerSites`, or ATS-matching `searchUrls` the run is rejected as described in [Limitations](#limitations). Alongside other platforms it is skipped with a logged reason.

`keywords`, `location`, `postedWithinDays`, and `sortBy` are forwarded to all three sub-actors and applied server-side before the per-company cap and before charging. When a company's jobs legitimately do not match, its `per_platform[]` entry carries a `company_notes[]` line such as `"Mayo Clinic: 540 jobs on the site, none matched nurse + London (filtered on the site)"`, and it is not retried through the browser.

#### Zero-job company rows

A company whose career site was read successfully but has no open roles, or none matching your filters, is surfaced as one dataset row with `_type: "company_no_matching_jobs"`. It carries the company (`name`, `domain`, `url`, `career_page_url`, `ats_detected`), `jobs_on_site`, `jobs_matching: 0`, a `reason` (`no_jobs_found`, `filtered_out_by_filters`, or `no_location_match_on_site`), a `note`, the active `filters`, and `scraped_at`. These rows are never charged and do not count toward `unique_jobs`. A company that delivered even one job row never also gets one. A site that could not be read at all (blocked, DNS failure, parked domain, JS-heavy page with no successful browser retry) produces no zero-job row either, only a note or warning, and is not charged. Apify dataset views only choose columns, not rows, so filter in your own code or the Console search box.

`jobs_on_site` is a number only when the site-wide total is really known. It is `null` when the ATS search already applied your filter server-side, because the reported count then describes the filtered search, and `note` says so. Turn `includeCompaniesWithoutJobs` off for job rows only, or filter in your own code: job rows have no `_type`, zero-job rows have `_type == "company_no_matching_jobs"`.

#### Picking HTTP or browser

For URLs that match no known ATS, the mode follows which extractors you name in `platforms[]`:

| `platforms` names | Mode | What happens |
|---|---|---|
| `website-job-extractor` only | HTTP only | No browser retry. A JS-rendered page returns a zero-row reason telling you to add the browser variant. |
| `website-job-extractor-browser` only | Browser only | Every non-ATS URL goes straight to a real browser, roughly 3-5x the HTTP rate. |
| Both or neither (**default**) | HTTP first, scoped retry | Only companies flagged as JS-rendered, or with zero jobs and no better explanation, are re-sent through the browser. Companies that returned jobs, or whose zero is explained by your own filters, are never re-sent or double-charged. |

The legacy `enableBrowserFallback: true` forces the default mode; new inputs should use `platforms`. The scoped retry gets `max(subactorTimeoutSecs, 1800)` seconds, capped by the run's remaining time minus a 90 second reserve. If it times out, job-feed gracefully aborts it and keeps the rows already pushed, with status `TIMED-OUT`. The original platform's zero-row reason is replaced by the retry's real outcome (`browser retry found 0 jobs`, `browser retry timed out ...`, `browser retry failed: ...`). If HTTP and the retry both touch a company, the browser's outcome decides: if it finds jobs there is no zero-job row.

#### Handing a job system to the next run

Job rows read through a known ATS carry `ats_system` and `ats_url`. job-feed uses them to build `next_run_input` in the OUTPUT record: each company whose job system was found moves from `companyUrls` to a `careerSites` entry (with `company` set to your original domain), and the rest stay in `companyUrls`. It carries only `{companyUrls, careerSites}` (plus a short `next_run_input_note`), so merge those two fields into your input and keep your own limits: pasted on its own with no limits, each career site is read in full instead of capped like the first run. A company left with no usable URL after cleanup stays in `companyUrls`. Those companies then read straight through `career-site-jobs`, same jobs, lower cost. The same handover fires from the extractor's per-company summary row, which covers a JS-rendered company with zero jobs whose job system was still identified. A company with several sites on one system gets one entry per site, and a Phenom tenant under several locales is collapsed to one URL per host (preferring `/global/en`). `icims` and `goldman_sachs` are never handed over because `career-site-jobs` cannot read them; `icims_jibe` is, always named explicitly.

Example: a first run with `companyUrls: ["https://www.kenvue.com/careers"]` discovers Workday and returns

```json
{
  "companyUrls": [],
  "careerSites": [
    {"url": "https://kenvue.wd1.myworkdayjobs.com/en-US/kenvue_careers", "ats": "workday", "company": "kenvue.com"}
  ]
}
```

Cost example, Chewy (about 264 roles, on Phenom): first run via `website-job-extractor` managed is about $3.20 (264 x $0.012 plus $0.01/company); every later run via `career-site-jobs` is about $0.27 (264 x $0.001).

#### Managed LLM key

Without your own `openrouterApiKey`, job-feed forwards no key into `website-job-extractor` runs. It tags the run with NanoScrape's managed key profile, and the extractor resolves the key server-side and bills at its own managed rate, see that actor's README for current prices and caps. Supplying `openrouterApiKey` (or the `geminiApiKey` / `groqApiKey` fallbacks) switches the run to standard billing on your own account.

### Location and language

**`location`** is free text and most boards accept it as-is. Boards with a closed list, or no location field, are resolved by job-feed when possible:

- **`swissdevjobs-ch`** - accepts only its own city names (`"Zurich"`, not `"Zürich"`); job-feed matches case- and accent-insensitively.
- **`arbeit-swiss`** - 2-letter canton code, resolved from any of the 26 cantons or their main cities.
- **`sozjobs-ch`** - 7 German-Swiss macro-regions (`zurich`, `berne`, `east`, `northwest`, `mittelland`, `central`, `graubunden`) via the canton; French and Italian cantons intentionally resolve to no match.
- **`alpha-topjobs-ch`** - 6 JobCloud region IDs; Zurich, Basel, Bern, Geneva get their own, other cantons a coarse bucket, Ticino none.
- **`lavoro-cdt-ch`** - Ticino only, 4 districts: Lugano, Mendrisio, Locarno, Chiasso (no Bellinzona, the sub-actor does not offer it).
- **`healthecareers-us`** - full US state name; abbreviations and `"City, ST"` are resolved.
- **`craigslist-jobs`** - regional site slugs for a curated set of major metros.
- **`jobs-ch`**, **`ictjobs-ch`**, and the three company-site actors take free text as-is.
- **`ge-ch-emploi`** has no location field and lists only Geneva roles.

When a mapping fails, or the board has no location field, job-feed logs a warning and post-filters that board's rows instead: rows whose own location text does not contain your `location` are dropped, never billed, and counted as `dropped_off_location`. Rows flagged remote are kept when they name no country or a matching one. Rows with no location data are dropped. This only triggers when you set `location`, and never on top of a successful native filter. The three company-site actors are always post-filtered as a safety net because each processes many companies per call; it normally drops nothing.

**`language`** on each row is inferred. Swiss listings use a canton heuristic (Geneva, Vaud, Fribourg, Neuchatel, Jura, Valais to `fr`, Ticino to `it`, else `de`); otherwise a country-to-language table (`DE`/`AT` to `de`, `FR` to `fr`, `US`/`GB`/`CA`/`AU`/`IE`/`IN`/`PK` to `en`, and about 20 more); otherwise a conservative stopword guess over title and description. With no signal it is `""`, never a default `"de"`.

### Dedup mode

- **`streaming`** (default) - rows are pushed as each board finishes. The first board to report a `job_id` owns the row, later reports go into `sources_manifest` under `additional_sources_by_job_id`. `sources[]` has length 1. Best for real-time use, fastest first result, and aborts (you pay only for rows already delivered).
- **`batch`** - rows are buffered until all boards finish, then emitted once per `job_id` with every reporting board in `sources[]`. No partial delivery if the run is killed, slower first result, more memory.

Billing is identical: one `orchestrator-unique-job` event per unique `job_id`. See [How job IDs and dedup work](#how-job-ids-and-dedup-work).

### Advanced concurrency

- **`maxParallelPlatforms`** - sub-actor runs kept in flight at once (default 8, 1-32). Apify's concurrent-run limit is account-wide, so job-feed lowers this cap to fit your account's limit (a free account runs 3 at a time). A `402 concurrent-runs-limit-exceeded` on start is retried with backoff (5s to 60s), and if some of job-feed's own runs are still going it keeps waiting for one of them to finish instead of giving up.
- **`perHostConcurrency`** - concurrent runs sharing a host (default 2, max 6).
- **`globalConcurrency`** - legacy in-flight cap (default 0, max 16). If both it and `maxParallelPlatforms` are set, the lower wins.
- **`maxTotalMemoryMbytes`** - sub-actor RAM budget, 0 = 4096 MB. See [RAM and parallelism](#ram-and-parallelism).
- **`subactorTimeoutSecs`** - per-board timeout (default 600, 60-3600). The scoped browser retry has its own longer budget.

### Partial failure and statusMessage

When a run finishes, `statusMessage` summarizes it, for example `"14/14 platforms succeeded"`, or names the failed boards. It also carries the dedup summary, a short reason when a healthy board returned nothing, the count of zero-job company rows (`"... + 2 companies with no matching jobs"`), and any `dropped_over_cap` count. Partial failure still ends `SUCCEEDED` with every job the working boards returned.

A board job-feed stops waiting on (its poll budget or Apify's timeout ran out) is gracefully aborted and its already-pushed rows are kept through normal dedup and billing. Its `per_platform[]` entry reports `status: "TIMED-OUT"` with the salvaged `raw_results` and a `reason` such as `"timed out after 30 min; kept 12 row(s) collected before the cut-off"`. It counts as neither succeeded nor failed, and never fails the run if at least one real row was delivered and billed. `statusMessage` then reads like `"0/1 platforms succeeded (1 board(s) timed out, rows kept: website-job-extractor-browser)"`, never with the `"FAILED: "` prefix.

**Approaching the run timeout**, boards that cannot usefully start are skipped (`SKIPPED_DEADLINE`) and running boards are stopped shortly before the deadline so rows can be salvaged. `statusMessage` then reads like `"Stopped before the run timeout: 4 of 6 boards finished, 2 stopped early (rows kept). Increase the run timeout for complete results."`, and `run_summary.stopped_for_deadline` is `true` with `deadline_stopped_boards`. The run is `SUCCEEDED`. See [Run timeout](#run-timeout).

Two cases end `FAILED` with `statusMessage` starting `"FAILED: "`, told apart by exit code:

- **Exit code 2, nothing dispatched.** The selection was rejected at validation (only URL-only platforms and no URL). Nothing is billed.
- **Exit code 1, every dispatched platform failed and nothing was delivered.** `statusMessage` names the failed platforms.

Both exist so an all-failed run never looks like a successful run with no results. A board that only finished via a salvaged `TIMED-OUT` run does not count as succeeded here, but if it delivered and billed a real row the run is not failed on that basis.

### LLM keys

All optional, used only when a URL is routed to `website-job-extractor` or its browser variant. Leave them blank for managed mode (see [Managed LLM key](#managed-llm-key)). The forced primary model is `deepseek/deepseek-chat-v3-0324`.

- **`openrouterApiKey`** - primary key, standard BYOK billing on your account.
- **`geminiApiKey`** - cross-provider fallback, used only if the whole OpenRouter side fails.
- **`groqApiKey`** - second fallback (Llama-3.3-70b), after Gemini.

### Terminal items in the OUTPUT record

Every run produces four `_type`-tagged items: `run_summary`, `cost_report`, `relevance_report`, `sources_manifest`. By default they live only in the run's **OUTPUT key-value-store record**, next to a live-updated `subruns[]` manifest (one entry per board: `actor`, `actor_id`, `build_tag`, `build_number`, `run_id`, `console_url`, `dataset_id`, `status`, `started_at`, timing, memory, charged amount), updated as boards finish. If the run had `companyUrls` or `careerSites`, OUTPUT also carries `next_run_input`. Set `includeReportRowsInDataset: true` to also append the four items to the dataset; if you export to CSV or Excel, drop rows with a non-empty `_type` (or keep only rows that have a `job_id`), since they do not share the job schema.

- **`run_summary`** - totals, `dedup_summary`, `completeness` (`all_platforms_succeeded`, `platforms_failed_count`), and `per_platform[]` with `platform_id`, `status`, `raw_results`, `elapsed_ms`, plus when relevant `country` (global-board sub-runs), `reason` (why a healthy board returned 0, with a generic fallback when the board gave none), `dropped_over_cap`, and `dropped_off_location` (only on boards without a server-side location filter, such as `ge-ch-emploi`). The two `dropped_*` counts also appear at top level as sums. Also `companies_not_read` (with `companies_not_read_count`), the list of requested `careerSites` and `companyUrls` entries that gave no jobs because they could not be read (each with `company`, `url`, `platform_id`, `reason` and `detail`, for example an unusable link, a blocked site, or a sub-run that failed to start), which marks the run INCOMPLETE in `completeness` when a sub-run failed; also `companies_without_jobs`, and on early stops `stopped_for_deadline` and `deadline_stopped_boards`.
- **`cost_report`** - `total_cost_usd` and a `per_platform[]` breakdown, see [Billing and cost model](#billing-and-cost-model).
- **`relevance_report`** - per-board on-topic rate, a hint to drop boards that return off-topic rows.
- **`sources_manifest`** - cross-board origins for jobs seen on several boards (streaming mode).

## How job IDs and dedup work

`job_id` is the first 16 hex characters of `SHA-256(foldText(title) | foldText(company) | foldText(city))`. A job with no city uses region and country instead, so remote listings do not collide on an empty city. The same job at the same company in the same city hashes identically from any board, today or next month. Upsert on it.

`foldText` normalizes case, whitespace, umlauts, gender suffixes (`(m/w/d)`, `(f/m/x)`, `(a)`, `:in`), trailing workload markers (`", 80-100%"`), and dash variants.

Cross-board matches are folded into one row. **Same-board** postings with identical folded title, company, and city are never merged: every posting after the first gets an 8-hex suffix from its own `source_id` (`b39d05cf0914e480` and `b39d05cf0914e480-2e000388`). Two distinct USAJOBS "Accountant (Staff)" postings at Fort Belvoir are a real case. Measured on 613 rows over 7 DACH boards (2026-08-24): false-merge rate about 0%, false-split rate about 4%.

Every run's `run_summary` and `statusMessage` carry a line like

```
12 rows from boards → 11 unique jobs (1 merged: arbeit-swiss ×1)
```

The parenthetical lists boards that contributed merged rows, most first. On a `companyUrls` run it can also show trimmed rows: `29 rows from boards → 12 unique jobs (0 merged, 17 over cap)`.

## Billing and cost model

job-feed bills exactly one event, `orchestrator-unique-job`, per unique job delivered after dedup and `maxResultsTotal`. Rows dropped before delivery (caps, `titleFilter`, `postedWithinDays`, location post-filter, zero-job rows) are never billed by job-feed.

Every board job-feed fans out to is a separate actor with its own pay-per-event rates (SERP scans, detail fetches, contacts, LLM extraction), billed independently to the same Apify account at the same rate as running it standalone. Each sub-run appears on https://console.apify.com/actors/runs, and the OUTPUT record's `subruns[]` carries a `console_url` per board. A sub-actor may bill its own events for rows job-feed later trims. On `companyUrls` and `careerSites` runs the sub-actor's company fee applies whenever the career site was read successfully, even with no open jobs. Sites that could not be read are not charged. "Read successfully" covers a genuinely empty career page, jobs that exist but do not match your filters, and ordinary delivered rows. This fee belongs to the sub-actor, not to job-feed's `orchestrator-unique-job` event.

The `cost_report` separates what compute cost from what you were billed:

- **`per_platform[].user_charged_usd`** - what the board charged you, from its tier-resolved price per event times event count, re-read up to 3 times, 10 seconds apart (45-second budget), to absorb Apify's charged-event lag.
- **`per_platform[].charges_final`** - `true` if that re-check converged. `false` means the budget ran out and the figure may be a slight undercount.
- **`per_platform[].price_basis`** - `""` normally, `"free_tier"` when a tiered-only event was priced at the conservative FREE tier, `"actor_fallback"` when the sub-run had no pricing info. Either means a conservative estimate.
- **`per_platform[].estimated_cost_usd`** - registry-based fallback, used only when `user_charged_usd` cannot be computed.
- **`per_platform[].platform_compute_usd`** - the sub-run's CU cost, for internal monitoring, unrelated to your bill (0 if unavailable).
- **`subactor_cost_total_usd`**, **`orchestrator_cost_usd`** (`unique_jobs x $0.0005`), **`total_cost_usd`** (their sum) and **`cost_per_unique_job_usd`**.
- **`overlap_matrix`** / **`redundancy_hint`** - which boards return the same jobs, and which to drop without losing coverage.

`total_cost_usd` is never derived from `platform_compute_usd`. Tiered boards (`stepstone-de`, `jobs-ch`) charge less on higher Apify plans: `user_charged_usd` uses your run's actual tier where it could be resolved, and `price_basis: "free_tier"` marks entries priced at the conservative FREE tier instead.

## Rate card

| Event | Trigger | Price |
|---|---|---|
| `orchestrator-unique-job` | Each unique job emitted after dedup and the optional `maxResultsTotal` cap | $0.0005 |

Sub-actor events are billed by the sub-actors on top, see [Supported boards](#supported-boards). A typical run of 3 boards x 2 keywords x `maxResultsPerQueryPerPlatform=25` yields about 100-110 unique jobs, so about $0.055 of orchestrator fee. Lean HTTP boards cost roughly $0.003/job and browser-tier boards $0.012-$0.020/job, so budget about $0.40-$0.80 all-in for 100 jobs without detail fetch. A real DE-Munich Software Engineer run over 4 boards (25 SERP rows each, no detail fetch) gave 87 raw rows, 85 unique jobs, $0.478 sub-actor subtotal plus $0.042 orchestrator fee: $0.522 total, $0.006 per unique job.

The single country, multiple countries, multi-keyword, cross-platform merge, and per-company cap examples come from real production runs, with output trimmed.

### Single country

```json
{"countries": ["CH"], "keywords": ["software engineer"]}
```

With `includeGlobalBoards` on, this fires 6 boards: the CH preset (`jobs-ch`, `arbeit-swiss`, `jobscout24-ch`) plus `indeed`, `glassdoor`, and `linkedin` scoped to CH. Real run: 36 raw rows, 36 unique jobs, 0 merged. Only the three global boards carry `country: "CH"` in `per_platform[]`.

```json

`jobs-ch` takes `"Zürich"` as free text, `arbeit-swiss` resolves it to canton `ZH`, `jobscout24-ch` to its own region enum, and the global boards pass it as free text. ```json
{"_type": "sources_manifest", "additional_sources_by_job_id": {
  "8d885572d84c4142": [{"platform": "arbeit-swiss", "url": "https://www.job-room.ch/job-search/92d43f2e-1b0e-4cc9-8495-a012b169b357", "company_name": "LHH"}]}}
```

The summary reads `12 rows from boards → 11 unique jobs (1 merged: arbeit-swiss ×1)`.

### Per-company cap with an over-cap trim

```json
{"companyUrls": ["https://boards.greenhouse.io/stripe", "https://jobs.lever.co/figma"], "maxResultsPerPlatform": 6}
```

Both route to `career-site-jobs`, and the cap splits as `floor(6/2)=3` per company (`maxJobsPerCompany: 3`). A real run that also added `https://www.python.org/jobs/` (extractor, 23 jobs on one page) kept 6 of them and trimmed 17: `29 rows from boards → 12 unique jobs (0 merged, 17 over cap)`. Only the 12 kept jobs are billed by job-feed, each affected `per_platform[]` entry carries its share as `dropped_over_cap`, though a sub-actor may have billed its own events for the trimmed rows.

### Tight budget

```json
{"countries": ["DE"], "keywords": ["software engineer"], "includeGlobalBoards": false,
 "maxResultsPerQueryPerPlatform": 5, "maxResultsTotal": 20, "maxTotalMemoryMbytes": 700, "maxParallelPlatforms": 2}
```

Limits RAM and volume at once. Four DE boards request 512 MB each and `stepstone-de` 128 MB (2176 MB in total), so under a 700 MB budget only some start at once and the rest queue, largest fitting request first, with at most 2 in flight.

## FAQ

**Why did I get fewer results than my cap?** Caps are upper bounds. A board may have fewer matches, and dedup and `maxResultsTotal` trim further. Compare `run_summary.per_platform[].raw_results` with `dedup_summary`.

**Why did a board return 0 jobs?** A `SUCCEEDED` board with `raw_results: 0` always carries a `reason` in its `per_platform[]` entry (no matches, rate limit, failed location mapping, and so on).

**Why does my company career page return zero jobs?** If the URL matched a known ATS it went to `career-site-jobs`, check its `reason`. Otherwise it went to `website-job-extractor`, and a JS-only page may need the browser variant, see [Picking HTTP or browser](#picking-http-or-browser).

**Why did the run fail instead of returning partial results?** Partial failure ends `SUCCEEDED`. Only a total failure, or a selection of URL-only platforms with no URL, ends `FAILED`, see [Partial failure and statusMessage](#partial-failure-and-statusmessage).

**How do I avoid duplicates across runs?** `job_id` is stable, so upsert on it. job-feed merges duplicates within a run but keeps no memory between runs.

**Where are run_summary and the other reports?** In the OUTPUT key-value-store record, not the dataset, unless `includeReportRowsInDataset` is on, see [Terminal items in the OUTPUT record](#terminal-items-in-the-output-record).

**Does the US preset include Indeed?** Yes, through `includeGlobalBoards` (default on). With it off, the US preset is `usajobs-us`, `wellfound-us`, and `workatastartup-us`.

**Does it work on the Free plan?** Yes. With `maxTotalMemoryMbytes` at 0 the sub-actor budget fits every plan. Boards that do not fit queue instead of failing, see [RAM and parallelism](#ram-and-parallelism).

**Does `location` apply to remote jobs?** A remote row matches when it names no country, or a country matching your location's. A remote row naming a different country is dropped and counted in `dropped_off_location`. See [Location and language](#location-and-language).

**How long does a run take?** From under a minute for a few lean boards to several minutes for a large multi-country preset. The default Apify timeout is 3600 seconds, raise it for big selections. On timeout job-feed stops gracefully and keeps collected rows, see [Run timeout](#run-timeout).

**What exactly am I charged for?** `orchestrator-unique-job` at $0.0005 per delivered unique job, plus each sub-actor's own events, see [Billing and cost model](#billing-and-cost-model). Dropped rows are not billed by job-feed, though the sub-actor may already have billed its own event for them.

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `FAILED`, exit code 2, nothing dispatched | Only URL-only platforms selected, with no `companyUrls`, `careerSites`, or `searchUrls` | Add a URL, or select keyword-driven boards too, the `statusMessage` names the fix |
| `FAILED`, exit code 1, after some boards ran | Every dispatched board failed (rate limits, timeouts, sub-actor errors) | Read `statusMessage` for each failure reason |
| `career-site-jobs` is `SKIPPED_NO_INPUT` but the run `SUCCEEDED` | Mixed selection without a URL for it | Expected, add `companyUrls` or `careerSites` if you wanted ATS results |
| Fewer rows than expected from a preset | `includeGlobalBoards` is off, or a board returned 0 that day | Check `per_platform[].reason` on the zero-row board |
| `website-job-extractor` returned 0 on a custom page | JS-rendered page (`js_rendering_suspected`) | Add `website-job-extractor-browser` to `platforms`, see [Picking HTTP or browser](#picking-http-or-browser) |
| Two different jobs share a `job_id` prefix | Same-board collision, correctly disambiguated | Look for the `-XXXXXXXX` suffix, both are real postings |
| `location` seems ignored on one board | Closed location list or no location field | Look for a `location does not match` warning in the log, see [Location and language](#location-and-language) |
| `titleFilter` or `postedWithinDays` seems not to apply | Filtered client-side after fetch on most boards | Check `dropped_title_filter` and `dropped_stale` on `run_summary` |
| A cap seems ignored | Misspelled or aliased field name | Look for `WARN input contains unrecognized keys` |
| `user_charged_usd` is 0 or low on a board that returned jobs | Apify charged-event lag right after the run | Check `charges_final`, re-fetch that sub-run later, `estimated_cost_usd` is the fallback |
| `price_basis` is `"free_tier"` or `"actor_fallback"` | Informational, a conservative price estimate was used | Nothing to fix |
| Same job appears twice across two runs | `job_id` is stable, but job-feed keeps no memory between runs | Upsert on `job_id` in your own storage |
| A board you expected is not in the preset | It is Tier 2 for that country | Add it via `platforms[]` |

## Registry

`registry/platforms.json` is the single source of truth. Status values: `healthy` (in country defaults), `degraded` and `unvalidated` (only when named explicitly), `parked` (pulled, never runs), `excluded` (deliberately never selectable). A platform can also carry `release: "coming_soon"`: built and routed, but its Apify actor is not public yet, so it is excluded from the `platforms` enum and country defaults.

To add or remove a board, run these from `actors/jobs/job-feed/`, then `apify push`:

1. `python3 scripts/refresh_registry_from_apify.py` - refreshes `subactor_registry.json` from live Apify data.
2. `python3 scripts/sync_platform_enum.py` - regenerates the `platforms` enum and `enumTitles` in `.actor/input_schema.json` from the registry.
3. `python3 scripts/gen_coming_soon.py` - regenerates the [Coming soon](#coming-soon) section.
4. `python3 scripts/gen_board_table.py` - regenerates the [Supported boards](#supported-boards) table.

## Run job-feed from code

job-feed is `santamaria-automations/job-feed` (actor ID `zoDyIgISr7yFPyLJd`). Any of the three client SDKs or a plain HTTP call can start it; a run can take a few minutes once several boards are involved, so prefer starting it and getting a webhook when it finishes over blocking a request while it runs. See [Get notified when a run finishes (webhook)](#get-notified-when-a-run-finishes) below.

**curl**, starting a run and polling for it yourself:

```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.apify.com/v2/acts/santamaria-automations~job-feed/runs?token=$APIFY_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"countries":["GB"],"keywords":["accountant","nurse"],"maxResultsPerQueryPerPlatform":40}'
```

That returns the run's `id` and `defaultDatasetId` right away, before the boards finish. You can address the same actor by ID instead of the `owner~name` slug: `POST /v2/acts/zoDyIgISr7yFPyLJd/runs`. Poll `GET /v2/actor-runs/{runId}` until `status` is `SUCCEEDED` (or `FAILED`/`TIMED-OUT`/`ABORTED`), then read the dataset:

```bash
curl "https://api.apify.com/v2/datasets/{defaultDatasetId}/items?token=$APIFY_TOKEN"
```

**JavaScript** (`apify-client`):

```js
import { ApifyClient } from 'apify-client';

const client = new ApifyClient({ token: process.env.APIFY_TOKEN });

// .call() starts the run and blocks until it finishes, convenient for a
// script or a short cron job, but it ties up the connection for as long
// as the run takes.
const run = await client.actor('santamaria-automations/job-feed').call({
    countries: ['GB'],
    keywords: ['accountant', 'nurse'],
    maxResultsPerQueryPerPlatform: 40,
});

// .start() returns immediately with the run object; pair it with a
// webhook (below) instead of polling when you can.
// const run = await client.actor('santamaria-automations/job-feed').start({ ... });

const { items } = await client.dataset(run.defaultDatasetId).listItems();
const output = await client.keyValueStore(run.defaultKeyValueStoreId).getRecord('OUTPUT');
console.log(items.length, 'rows,', output.value.subruns.length, 'boards ran');
```

**Python** (`apify-client`):

```python
from apify_client import ApifyClient

client = ApifyClient(token=os.environ["APIFY_TOKEN"])

# call() blocks until the run finishes; start() returns immediately, use it
# with a webhook instead of polling for anything long-running.
run = client.actor("santamaria-automations/job-feed").call(run_input={
    "countries": ["GB"],
    "keywords": ["accountant", "nurse"],
    "maxResultsPerQueryPerPlatform": 40,
})

items = client.dataset(run["defaultDatasetId"]).list_items().items
output = client.key_value_store(run["defaultKeyValueStoreId"]).get_record("OUTPUT")
print(len(items), "rows,", len(output["value"]["subruns"]), "boards ran")
```

### Get notified when a run finishes

**From the Console:** open https://console.apify.com/actors/zoDyIgISr7yFPyLJd/integrations, add an HTTP webhook, set it to fire when the run condition is "Run succeeded" (add "Run failed", "Run timed out", and "Run aborted" too if you want to be notified of those as well), and point it at `YOUR_WEBHOOK_URL`. Leave the payload template at Apify's default, or set it explicitly to:

```json
{
    "userId": {{userId}},
    "createdAt": {{createdAt}},
    "eventType": {{eventType}},
    "eventData": {{eventData}},
    "resource": {{resource}}
}
```

`resource` is the full run object at the moment the event fired, so `resource.defaultDatasetId` and `resource.defaultKeyValueStoreId` are what you need to go fetch the job rows and the `OUTPUT` record above, the same two IDs you'd otherwise get back from `.start()` or the run-creation API call.

A minimal receiver, Node/Express:

```js
app.post('/job-feed-webhook', express.json(), async (req, res) => {
    res.sendStatus(200); // ack immediately, then process
    const { eventType, resource } = req.body;
    if (eventType !== 'ACTOR.RUN.SUCCEEDED') return;
    const output = await client.keyValueStore(resource.defaultKeyValueStoreId).getRecord('OUTPUT');
    // ... handle output.value.subruns, fetch resource.defaultDatasetId items, etc.
});
```

or Python/Flask:

```python
@app.route("/job-feed-webhook", methods=["POST"])
def job_feed_webhook():
    body = request.get_json()
    if body["eventType"] == "ACTOR.RUN.SUCCEEDED":
        resource = body["resource"]
        output = client.key_value_store(resource["defaultKeyValueStoreId"]).get_record("OUTPUT")
        # ... handle output["value"]["subruns"], fetch resource["defaultDatasetId"] items, etc.
    return "", 200
```

The event types Apify fires are `ACTOR.RUN.CREATED`, `ACTOR.RUN.SUCCEEDED`, `ACTOR.RUN.FAILED`, `ACTOR.RUN.ABORTED`, `ACTOR.RUN.TIMED_OUT`, and `ACTOR.RUN.RESURRECTED`.

Instead of (or alongside) a standing Console webhook, you can attach one to a single run at start time with the `webhooks` query parameter: a base64-encoded JSON array of `{eventTypes, requestUrl, payloadTemplate}` objects, appended to the run-creation URL:

```bash
WEBHOOKS=$(echo -n '[{"eventTypes":["ACTOR.RUN.SUCCEEDED","ACTOR.RUN.FAILED","ACTOR.RUN.TIMED_OUT"],"requestUrl":"https://your-app.example.com/job-feed-webhook"}]' | base64)
curl -X POST "https://api.apify.com/v2/acts/santamaria-automations~job-feed/runs?token=$APIFY_TOKEN&webhooks=$WEBHOOKS" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"countries":["GB"],"keywords":["accountant","nurse"]}'
```

### Run timeout

The default run timeout is 3600 seconds (1 hour), set under Run options in the Console or with the `timeout` query parameter on the run-creation API call, for example `?timeout=7200` for 2 hours. If the boards you selected need more than the default to finish, raise it rather than letting the run cut off, since a large `countries`/`keywords` combination with several boards and `includeJobDetails: true` can legitimately take longer than an hour.

If the timeout is reached anyway, job-feed does not leave sub-runs orphaned: boards still running are stopped gracefully with their rows kept (see [Partial failure and statusMessage](#partial-failure-and-statusmessage)), boards that never got a chance to start are skipped, and the run still ends `SUCCEEDED` with whatever it managed to collect, rather than being torn down mid-flight with nothing saved.
